text:
Alex: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector change we see a small but reproducible quality drift on the Mistral-family canary (mixtral-7b variant) in the nightly evals.
Maya: Noted. Which change exactly? the tiled-attn fallback or the new fused-kv path?
Alex: Fused attention kernel got prioritized for short-seq paths. Selector picked it for many chat traces. We also flipped a RoPE scaling tweak in the same rollout.
Sam K.: I just pulled profiler traces. Latency improved ~6% P50 but attention operator shows higher output divergence on our metrics (BLEU-ish task + safety checks). KV cache churn up ~12% for some prompts.
Jin: Can you paste the trace snippet?
Sam K.: Sure — here's the noisy part:
```
# perf summary (shortened)
attn_fused_forward: 38ms -> 29ms (P50)
kv_cache_apply: 6.2ms -> 7.0ms (hot spots)
mem_copy_kv: +18% throughput
quantize_post: no change
```
Alex: The evasion in QA diffs looks like token ordering for long-range references — points to RoPE boundary scaling mismatch.
Maya: We did reduce RoPE wrap factor to avoid saturation with tiled-attn. That could shift phase and break a few hallucination heuristics.
QA Team: Failing tests: `core-doc-ref` and `temporal-coherence-3`. Diff snippet: top answer changed to older context snippet.
Sam K.: Reproduced locally with the same model + runtime config. If I force the old kernel selection the eval passes.
Jin: So two suspects: kernel swap + RoPE tweak. Which order do we rollback?
Maya: Rollback kernel first — cheaper, canary-scale flip is instant. If it fixes, we know kernel selection logic introduced subtle numeric differences (maybe fma vs reorder).
Alex: Agreed. Also create a job to re-run the quantization/regression harness with bit-exact compare on a subset.
Sam K.: I'll push a hotfix revert for the selector (PR #4217) and roll a canary.
perf-bot: Canary deploy started (deployment id: dpl-2026-03-18-07). Metrics will stream here.
Maya: Also add a focused probe that records per-head KV norms and RoPE phase for failing traces. We need concrete signals not just eval scores.
QA Team: Requesting the failing prompts and before/after logits for the top 8 tokens for the `core-doc-ref` suite.
Sam K.: Attaching short list to the issue — linking to internal gist: https://redwood.internal/g/encore/mt-suspect-traces (private).
Alex: After canary rollback, plan: 1) run canary evals, 2) run head-level KV norm histogram, 3) run long-context prompt battery. If still fails, revert RoPE change.
Jin: Also run the low-precision QA with quant toggles — last time we saw FP16 vs int8 rounding expose different ordering.
Maya: Note for followup: add a heuristic to avoid fused-attn for sequences where cached-kv reuse ratio < 0.5 (it increases mem-copy overhead). Could reduce churn.
perf-bot: Canary metrics: P50 down -> +6% improvement, eval-failure-rate bumped +0.9% on canary slice (20k requests) — monitoring.
QA Team: Canary rollback confirmed?
Sam K.: Canary halted and rolled back at 1799123578. Rolling back PR now.
Alex: Good. Assigning follow-ups: Sam -> revert PR + attach logs, Maya -> add KV/rope probe, Jin -> run quant comparison harness, QA -> re-run failing suites after rollback and report boolean pass/fail.
QA Team: Will run and report by EOD.
Maya: Filing a postmortem ticket with perf + eval diffs, linking to PR and canary metrics.
Alex: Thanks all. If QA passes after rollback we'll re-evaluate a safer selector rule with an explicit small canary and head-level assertions. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Postmortem ticket created: INC-9872. Canary snapshot archived: s3://redwood-canaries/1799123456/snapshot.tar.gz
QA Team: Verified — core-doc-ref and temporal-coherence-3 pass after rollback. Closing the immediate regression loop.
Sam K.: Follow-on idea: add a lightweight head-consistency check to the runtime that rejects kernel swap when head-wise cosine distance > 0.02 compared to baseline for same input.
Maya: Love that. We'll prototype as an opt-in runtime flag.
Alex: OK closing thread — thanks everyone.
